A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLARE research work. Their text, equations, seven tables, six figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original pose-estimation, reconstruction, novel-view synthesis, and ablation results, including additional DTU experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The pose predictor, two-stage geometry estimation, Gaussian appearance model, and training losses are unchanged. Naming gsplat in v7 documents the rendering implementation without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight training datasets and retain the same evaluation coverage, including RealEstate10K, DL3DV, ETH3D, DTU, TUM, and BlendedMVS. Appendix dense-view and variable-view scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the corresponding main-text and appendix experiments. RelPose and GeoMVSNet only receive new reference numbers; gsplat is identified as implementation software, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model sizes, metrics, splits, input-view selection, and testing procedures are unchanged. Examples include 200 training epochs, five-image RealEstate10K pose evaluation, and the appendix frame-count study with two fixed query views.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablations in Table 5, MVSplat input-view analysis in Figure 5, FLARE frame-count analysis in Table 6, and qualitative reconstruction examples. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands for the experiments. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–7 and the plotted and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, FLARE retains pose AUC@30° of 79.9 in Table 1, PSNR of 23.765 in Table 4, and dense-DTU overall error of 1.321 in Table 7.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(12), camera parametrization, geometry normalization, and loss definitions are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and discussion retain the same claims about cascaded learning, reconstruction from uncalibrated sparse views, performance, and inference within approximately 0.5 seconds.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are retained, including the rendering-loss accuracy/completeness tradeoff, diminishing gains from additional views, and weaker dense-DTU performance than MASt3R because FLARE targets sparse reconstruction.

D1.justification: Section 4 of v7 newly states that gsplat is used for efficient Gaussian splatting rendering. v5 describes a differentiable Gaussian rasterizer without naming this library. Other implementation details, Appendix A processing instructions, and the project/code link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v7 adds Ye et al.'s gsplat library paper as reference 94, supporting the new implementation attribution. Existing references are retained and subsequent entries renumbered; the research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The first author's name changes from Shangzan Zhang to Shangzhan Zhang, the version/date header updates, and one implementation sentence is added. Section organization and the remaining narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added sentence causes limited column reflow on page 6, and the added reference shifts bibliography content between pages 12–13. Figures, table structures, captions, and appendix layouts otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v7 modestly improves implementation transparency and attribution by naming and citing gsplat where v5 specified only a differentiable Gaussian rasterizer. This helps identify the software used for reproduction. The gain is limited: the scientific method, experimental evidence, interpretations, and limitations remain unchanged.
